A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NCV research. All 24 pages of v3 and 27 pages of v4, including Appendices A–G, support comparison of text, equations, tables and figures. Retained material can be matched across relocations.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, shortcut-learning experiments, architectural and mask-size ablations, and toy XOR/counting results.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds a comparison of concepts selected by NCV and a linear CBM on selected ImageNet classes.

M1.justification: The frozen concept extractors, cooperative and adversarial provers, verifier, rejection-aware losses, alternating continuous/hard-mask training, and inference procedure are retained. Rewriting Appendix A.4 and replacing agent terminology with module terminology do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CLEVR-Hans3/7, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, COCOLogic, and the toy XOR/counting tasks, including the same shortcut scenarios. The added ImageNet examples sample existing coverage rather than introduce a new task or environment.

E2.justification: Section E.5 adds a linear CBM comparator to the explanation analysis, which previously compared NCV with Pixel-MAC. Existing benchmark comparators, including DCR, remain unchanged. Section C.5 also supplies a literature-based V-IP comparison, explicitly distinguished from a controlled experiment.

E3.justification: The new explanation comparison uses six selected ImageNet classes, 32 test samples per class, and the five most frequently selected concepts on a shared vocabulary. Existing training budgets, splits, metrics and ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section E.5 and Table 11 examine whether NCV selects semantically meaningful concepts comparable to a linear CBM, including variation across images. Existing shortcut, mask-size, architecture and weighting-parameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 20 seeds for CLEVR-Hans, 10 for the main natural-image experiments, and three for the weighting-parameter analysis. Mean/standard-deviation reporting and Figure 5's averaging practice are unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores, ablation results, runtime estimates and plotted curves are unchanged. Table 11 adds concept lists and Section E.5 adds selection-frequency findings. Section C.5 newly quotes V-IP's approximately 60% accuracy after seven patch queries alongside NCV's retained 83.32%, under explicitly different feature settings.

T1.justification: The existing binary and one-vs-rest precision and mutual-information bounds are retained. Section 3.5 and Appendix A add explicit class-wise error definitions, sharpen concept-value containment, and introduce asserted feature-count upper bounds on asymmetric feature correlation. No new theorem or proof framework is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction contributions remain unchanged. The conclusion narrows v3's claim that NCV effectively mitigates shortcut learning to helping mitigate it when clean supervision is available.

C2.justification: v4 specifically distinguishes discrete NCB from continuous CLIP encodings when discussing estimability of theoretical precision. It also explains class-name overlap in the vocabulary and limits the new concept examples to deliberately selected successes. Broader noncausal and trained-adversary limitations already appeared in v3.

D1.justification: A new Software and Data statement supplies a repository location for the reported code and data; its actual availability is not established by the PDFs. Section E.5 newly discloses that class-name phrases were deliberately not filtered from the vocabulary. Existing implementation and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning through post-hoc CBMs, semantic-importance testing, sparse autoencoders and V-IP. New Section C.5 develops the V-IP relationship through differences in sequential versus single-step selection, representations, explanation forms and scalability. These additions extend the substantive discussion of neighboring approaches.

P1.justification: v4 substantially rewrites and reorganizes the theoretical exposition in Appendix A and adds a main-text theory summary in Section 3.5, moving training to Section 3.6. It expands background and setup explanations, adds C.5/E.5 and publication statements, and revises terminology and front matter.

P2.justification: v4 adds concept-comparison Table 11 and renumbers the retained runtime table to Table 12. Existing displays are regrouped, including Table 1 with Figure 3 and the two natural-image mask-size tables together. Figures 1–5 retain their graphics.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency by bringing theoretical qualifications into the main text, narrowing the shortcut conclusion, adding explicitly qualified concept comparisons, and providing code/data access information. Broader research positioning also helps readers assess the contribution. Gains remain limited: the main empirical evidence is retained, V-IP is not a controlled comparison, and Q4 still overstates the zero-clean-data result relative to Table 2.
